# exactl skill

A skill is a folder of instructions that a request can load. A new skill starts as a draft. Review it, then approve its revision to activate it.

## exactl skill list

List skills

Lists the skills of the current roots. `--all` also reports the folders that did not load.

**Usage:** `exactl skill list [options]`

**Options**

- `--category <category>`: Filter by category: core, project, learned (type: string)
- `--all`: Include diagnostics for folders that did not load
- `--portal <portal>`: Portal whose project skills apply. Without it only global skills apply (type: string)

**Examples**

List skills:

```bash
exactl skill list
```

List learned skills as JSON:

```bash
exactl skill list --category learned -o json
```

**Output:** collection.

**Exit codes**

- FAILURE (1)

**See also:** [exactl skill show](skill.md#exactl-skill-show), [exactl skill validate](skill.md#exactl-skill-validate)

## exactl skill show

Show a skill

Shows the current skill and its usage. `--revision` shows one stored revision instead.

**Usage:** `exactl skill show [options] <skill-id>`

**Arguments**

- `skill-id`

**Options**

- `--revision <revision>`: Show this stored revision instead of the current skill (type: string)
- `--portal <portal>`: Portal whose project skills apply. Without it only global skills apply (type: string)

**Examples**

Show a skill:

```bash
exactl skill show code-review
```

Show a stored revision:

```bash
exactl skill show code-review --revision <revision-uuid>
```

**Output:** item.

**Exit codes**

- FAILURE (1)
- USAGE (2)
- NOT_FOUND (3)

**See also:** [exactl skill revisions](skill.md#exactl-skill-revisions), [exactl skill list](skill.md#exactl-skill-list)

## exactl skill match

Match skills for a request

Ranks the skills whose triggers match the request text. Narrow it with a task type or tags.

**Usage:** `exactl skill match [options] <request>`

**Arguments**

- `request`

**Options**

- `--task-type <taskType>`: Task type filter (type: string)
- `--tags <tags>`: Comma-separated tags filter (type: string)
- `-n, --limit <limit>`: Maximum results (type: number, default: `10`)
- `--portal <portal>`: Portal whose project skills apply. Without it only global skills apply (type: string)

**Examples**

Match a request:

```bash
exactl skill match "review the pull request"
```

**Output:** collection.

**Exit codes**

- FAILURE (1)

**See also:** [exactl skill show](skill.md#exactl-skill-show), [exactl skill list](skill.md#exactl-skill-list)

## exactl skill derive

Derive a draft skill from learnings

Writes a draft skill from the listed learning ids. Review the draft, then approve its revision.

**Usage:** `exactl skill derive [options]`

**Options**

- `--learning-ids <ids>`: Comma-separated learning IDs to derive from (type: string, required)
- `--name <name>`: Name for the derived skill (type: string, required)
- `--description <desc>`: Skill description (type: string)
- `-i, --instructions <instructions>`: Skill instructions (type: string)
- `--portal <portal>`: Portal whose project skills apply. Without it only global skills apply (type: string)

**Examples**

Derive a skill:

```bash
exactl skill derive --learning-ids l1,l2 --name "Retry Handling"
```

**Output:** mutation.

**Exit codes**

- FAILURE (1)
- USAGE (2)
- NOT_FOUND (3)

**See also:** [exactl skill approve](skill.md#exactl-skill-approve), [exactl skill show](skill.md#exactl-skill-show)

## exactl skill create

Create a draft skill

Writes a draft skill. It is not active until you approve the revision you reviewed.

**Usage:** `exactl skill create [options] <name>`

**Arguments**

- `name`

**Options**

- `--description <desc>`: Skill description (type: string)
- `--category <category>`: Category: core, project, learned (type: string, default: `project`)
- `-i, --instructions <instructions>`: Skill instructions (type: string)
- `-k, --keywords <keywords>`: Comma-separated trigger keywords (type: string)
- `--task-types <taskTypes>`: Comma-separated trigger task types (type: string)
- `--portal <portal>`: Portal whose project skills apply. Without it only global skills apply (type: string)

**Examples**

Create a skill:

```bash
exactl skill create "Retry Handling" -i "Retry with backoff." -k retry,backoff
```

**Output:** mutation.

**Exit codes**

- FAILURE (1)
- USAGE (2)
- NOT_FOUND (3)

**See also:** [exactl skill approve](skill.md#exactl-skill-approve), [exactl skill show](skill.md#exactl-skill-show)

## exactl skill approve

Approve a reviewed skill revision

Activates the draft. The revision must be the one that was reviewed, or the command fails.

**Usage:** `exactl skill approve [options] <name>`

**Arguments**

- `name`

**Options**

- `--revision <revision>`: Revision UUID that was reviewed (type: string, required)
- `--portal <portal>`: Portal whose project skills apply. Without it only global skills apply (type: string)

**Examples**

Approve a revision:

```bash
exactl skill approve retry-handling --revision <revision-uuid>
```

**Output:** mutation.

**Exit codes**

- FAILURE (1)
- USAGE (2)
- NOT_FOUND (3)

**See also:** [exactl skill show](skill.md#exactl-skill-show), [exactl skill deprecate](skill.md#exactl-skill-deprecate)

## exactl skill deprecate

Take a skill out of matching

Stops the skill from matching. Approve a reviewed revision to bring it back.

**Usage:** `exactl skill deprecate [options] <name>`

**Arguments**

- `name`

**Options**

- `--portal <portal>`: Portal whose project skills apply. Without it only global skills apply (type: string)

**Examples**

Deprecate a skill:

```bash
exactl skill deprecate retry-handling
```

**Output:** mutation.

**Exit codes**

- FAILURE (1)
- USAGE (2)
- NOT_FOUND (3)

**See also:** [exactl skill approve](skill.md#exactl-skill-approve), [exactl skill revisions](skill.md#exactl-skill-revisions)

## exactl skill revisions

List the stored revisions of a skill

Lists every stored revision with its hash, first sighting and use counts.

**Usage:** `exactl skill revisions [options] <name>`

**Arguments**

- `name`

**Options**

- `--portal <portal>`: Portal whose project skills apply. Without it only global skills apply (type: string)

**Examples**

List revisions:

```bash
exactl skill revisions retry-handling
```

**Output:** collection.

**Exit codes**

- FAILURE (1)
- USAGE (2)
- NOT_FOUND (3)

**See also:** [exactl skill show](skill.md#exactl-skill-show), [exactl skill approve](skill.md#exactl-skill-approve)

## exactl skill usage

Show the skill usage of one trace

Lists every model call of the trace that carried a skill, joined to the revision it used.

**Usage:** `exactl skill usage [options]`

**Options**

- `--trace <trace>`: Trace id to read (type: string, required)
- `--portal <portal>`: Portal whose project skills apply. Without it only global skills apply (type: string)

**Examples**

Show usage:

```bash
exactl skill usage --trace 0b1c2d3e
```

**Output:** collection.

**Exit codes**

- FAILURE (1)
- USAGE (2)
- NOT_FOUND (3)

**See also:** [exactl skill revisions](skill.md#exactl-skill-revisions), [exactl skill show](skill.md#exactl-skill-show)

## exactl skill validate

Validate the skill roots

Reports the typed validation reasons for the current skill roots. It exits with a failure when a skill is invalid.

**Usage:** `exactl skill validate [options] [name]`

**Arguments**

- `name` (optional)

**Options**

- `--portal <portal>`: Portal whose project skills apply. Without it only global skills apply (type: string)

**Examples**

Validate every skill:

```bash
exactl skill validate
```

Validate one skill:

```bash
exactl skill validate retry-handling
```

**Output:** item.

**Exit codes**

- FAILURE (1)
- USAGE (2)
- NOT_FOUND (3)
- INVALID (6)

**See also:** [exactl skill list](skill.md#exactl-skill-list), [exactl skill show](skill.md#exactl-skill-show)
